name: Round Bar Weight Calculator
description: Calculate the weight of round steel bars and rods from diameter and length.

seo.title: Round Bar Weight Calculator - Steel Rod
seo.description: Round Bar Weight Calculator — Calculate the weight of round steel bars and rods from diameter and length with instant results & multiple unit support.

formula.explanation: Weight = π × (D/2)² × L × ρ. Cylinder volume times density. Diameter and length in meters after conversion.

content.introduction: Calculate the weight of a round bar or solid rod from its diameter and length. Used for steel reinforcing bars, shaft stock, and raw material ordering.

example.description: A 50mm diameter × 6m long carbon steel round bar weighs approximately 92.5 kg.

faq.q: What is the weight per meter of steel round bar?
faq.a: Weight per meter (kg/m) = π × (D/2)² × ρ. For 50mm steel: π × 0.000625 × 7850 ≈ 15.4 kg/m.
Yes, for plain round bars. Deformed rebar is typically 1-2% heavier due to ribs.

faq.q: What is the weight of a 12mm steel bar per meter?
faq.a: A 12mm diameter carbon steel round bar weighs approximately 0.888 kg/m (pi x 36 x 7850 / 1,000,000).

faq.q: What is the weight of a 20mm steel bar per meter?
faq.a: A 20mm diameter carbon steel round bar weighs approximately 2.47 kg/m. A standard 12m length weighs about 29.6 kg.

faq.q: How do I convert round bar weight from kg to pounds?
faq.a: Multiply the weight in kg by 2.20462. For example, 92.5 kg = 204 lb. For weight per meter, multiply kg/m by 0.67197 to get lb/ft.

faq.q: What is the difference between round bar and rebar weight?
faq.a: Plain round bar uses the exact cylinder formula. Deformed rebar is typically 1-2% heavier due to the surface ribs, so use a 1-2% uplift for rebar estimating.

sections.heading: Weight per Meter Reference (Carbon Steel)
sections.body:
Weight per meter for common round bar diameters (carbon steel, density 7850 kg/m3):
6 mm: 0.222 kg/m | 8 mm: 0.395 kg/m | 10 mm: 0.617 kg/m | 12 mm: 0.888 kg/m | 16 mm: 1.58 kg/m | 20 mm: 2.47 kg/m | 25 mm: 3.85 kg/m | 32 mm: 6.31 kg/m | 40 mm: 9.87 kg/m | 50 mm: 15.4 kg/m | 60 mm: 22.2 kg/m | 80 mm: 39.5 kg/m | 100 mm: 61.7 kg/m.
Formula: W (kg/m) = pi x (D/2)^2 x rho / 1,000,000 with D in mm and rho in kg/m3.

sections.heading: Worked Example: 20 mm Rebar
sections.body:
Estimate the weight of a 12 m long, 20 mm diameter carbon steel rebar.
Step 1 - cross-section area: A = pi x (20/2)^2 = 314.2 mm2 = 3.142 x 10^-4 m2.
Step 2 - volume: V = A x L = 3.142 x 10^-4 x 12 = 3.770 x 10^-3 m3.
Step 3 - weight: W = V x rho = 3.770 x 10^-3 x 7850 = 29.6 kg.
Check: 2.47 kg/m x 12 m = 29.6 kg. The bar weighs approximately 29.6 kg.

sections.heading: Unit Conversion Guide
sections.body:
Weight: 1 kg = 2.20462 lb; 1 tonne = 1000 kg = 2204.6 lb.
Weight per meter: 1 kg/m = 0.67197 lb/ft; 1 lb/ft = 1.488 kg/m.
Diameter: 1 mm = 0.03937 in; 1 in = 25.4 mm.
Length: 1 m = 3.281 ft.
Example: a 50 mm bar at 15.4 kg/m = 15.4 x 0.67197 = 10.35 lb/ft.
